In the [[mathematics]] of [[operator theory]], an [[linear operator|operator]] <math>A</math> on an ([[dimension (vector space)|infinite-dimensional]]) [[Banach space]] or [[Hilbert space]] <math>H</math> has a cyclic vector <math>f</math> if the vectors <math>f, Af, A^2f,\dots</math> [[spanning set|span]] <math>H</math>. Equivalently, <math>f</math> is a cyclic vector for <math>A</math> in case the set of all vectors of the form <math>p(A)f</math>, where <math>p</math> varies over all [[polynomial]]s, is [[dense set|dense]] in <math>H</math>.{{sfnp|Halmos|1982}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Cyclic vector |url=http://www.encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php?title=Cyclic_vector&oldid=34882 |website=Encyclopedia of Mathematics}}</ref>
